concerns.text: User Story 1 (P1, deterministic graph-based feature denoising) has FR-001 and FR-003 but NO success criterion anchored to it. All five SCs reference US-2 or US-3. The core P1 deliverable (denoised map achieves lower MSE than noisy input, CPU-only completion within time limit) has no SC-NNN, leaving the top-priority story without a measurable outcome.

The three Edge Cases state MUST-level behavior (disconnected-graph fallback to local smoothing; skipping/interpolating incomplete DA3 sequences; flagging null hypothesis results) but no FR covers any of them. These are silent under-specifications — the implementation has nothing concrete to build for the fallback or null-result handling.

FR-006 (paired t-test on reconstruction errors across 50 degraded scenes) is anchored '(See US-2)' but its content is the statistical validation of the US-3 performance comparison, not US-2's structural-property identification. Re-anchor to US-3 (or both) so traceability matches scope.

FR-006 (paired t-test on reconstruction errors across 50 degraded test scenes) is anchored '(See US-2)', but US-2 is the structural-property/correlation story; the paired t-test on the deterministic-vs-diffusion performance gap belongs to US-3 (whose journey explicitly covers comparative benchmarking). Cross-reference mismatch.

FR-007 (sensitivity analysis of the filter's cutoffs) is anchored '(See US-2)', but it concerns the US-1/US-3 filter parameters, not US-2's spectral analysis. Also 'false-positive/negative rates' is inconsistent terminology for a regression/denoising task measured by Chamfer Distance — no FR or SC defines a classification decision these rates would apply to.

FR-007 defers the sweep values ('k ∈ {representative low, medium, and high values}') while SC-004 pins concrete values 'k ∈ {5, 10, 15}'. Pick one convention so the FR and its success criterion describe the same sweep.

'a Chamfer Distance that is no more than 1.18x (approx. [deferred] efficiency)' mixes a hard-coded ratio (1.18x) with a [deferred] marker in the same clause. The 1.18x is a pre-asserted empirical threshold that contradicts the deferred-value convention stated in the Measurable Outcomes preamble; state the metric and reference (baseline CD) and defer the ratio.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-2 Acceptance Scenario 2 vs Edge Cases
concerns.text: US-2 scenario 2 mandates 'identifies at least one specific eigenmode... statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05)', while the Edge Cases section requires the system to 'flag the hypothesis as unsupported and record the null result' when no significant correlation exists. These are compatible only if the acceptance scenario is reframed as measuring the correlation (per SC-005) rather than guaranteeing a positive finding; as written the scenario asserts an empirical outcome.
Dataset is named 'Depth Anything 3 (DA3)' in the first assumption but 'the DA dataset' in the third assumption. Use one name consistently.

FR-007 requires reporting 'variation in false-positive/negative rates' for a denoising/reconstruction task. FP/FN rates are classification concepts with no defined decision boundary here — the implementer cannot know what counts as a false positive. Rewrite in terms of the actual metrics (e.g., variation in Chamfer Distance / MSE across the k and frequency-threshold sweep, consistent with SC-004).

'Then the system identifies at least one specific eigenmode... that shows a statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05)' demands a positive scientific outcome as an acceptance condition. The Edge Cases section correctly handles the null result, but this scenario as written is unfalsifiable-as-acceptance. Rephrase as a procedure: 'the system performs the correlation analysis and reports all eigenmode–robustness correlations with p-values', with the ≥85%/p<0.05 outcomes living in SC-001/SC-005 as measured hypotheses.

US-2 scenario 2 requires 'the system identifies at least one specific eigenmode or curvature metric that shows a statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05)'. This pre-asserts a positive scientific finding as an acceptance condition, contradicting the spec's own Edge Case ('flag the hypothesis as unsupported and record the null result'). The idea asks to *identify which properties correlate* — the outcome may be null. Rephrase as 'the system outputs the correlation analysis with p-values', not a guaranteed significant hit.

FR-007's sensitivity sweep reports 'variation in false-positive/negative rates' — FP/FN rates are a classification metric with no defined meaning for a denoising/reconstruction task measured in Chamfer Distance. The idea contains no such metric. State the sweep outcome in terms of the actual metrics (Chamfer Distance / F-score variation across k and frequency threshold).

FR-003 optimizes the filter 'via Mean Squared Error on CPU' against clean feature representations, and US-1 Scenario 2 validates the filter by 'lower Mean Squared Error (MSE) against the clean ground truth.' Validating on the same objective (and plausibly the same data) used to fit the filter is circular: a lower MSE than the noisy input is nearly guaranteed by any smoothing operator fit to that objective. Validation must use held-out scenes and a downstream metric (Chamfer/F-score), not the fitting objective.

'identifies at least one specific eigenmode or curvature metric that shows a statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05)' over the top-10 eigenvalues plus curvature metrics across 50 scenes. With ~10+ uncorrected tests, at least one p<0.05 hit is expected by chance (~40%+ probability). No multiple-comparison correction (e.g. Bonferroni/FDR) is specified, making the 'finding' near-unfalsifiable as stated.

The sensitivity analysis reports 'variation in false-positive/negative rates.' This is a denoising/regression pipeline with no classification labels; false-positive/negative rates are undefined here. The sweep should report variation in Chamfer Distance / F-score (the actual outcome metrics), not classification error rates.

Paired t-test on per-scene reconstruction errors: Chamfer distances are non-negative, right-skewed, and bounded, and per-scene errors may be heteroscedastic. A paired t-test on raw errors is fragile; the spec should either justify normality or specify a non-parametric alternative (e.g. Wilcoxon signed-rank) or log-transform, and state the direction of the hypothesis being tested.

'recovers ≥85% of the baseline's robustness' is operationalized as 'Chamfer Distance no more than 1.18x the baseline's.' This ratio definition is arbitrary and asymmetric (it ignores the noisy-input reference point); a more standard definition would interpolate between the no-filter (noisy) error and the diffusion baseline error. As written, the criterion is measurable but the mapping from '85% robustness' to '1.18x CD' is unjustified.

new_concerns.text: US-2 Scenario 1 states the system 'outputs a list of the top 10 eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors for each scene.' This is a data-collection requirement, not a validation of the hypothesis. The spec does not state HOW these spectral properties will be used to identify 'robust structural signatures' or what constitutes a 'robust' signature. The connection between computed eigenvalues and the denoising filter design (FR-003) is missing — is the filter parameterized BY these eigenmodes, or is the spectral analysis purely exploratory?

SC-002 defines success as 'Chamfer Distance no more than 1.18x the diffusion baseline's distance.' However, the spec does not state whether this comparison is on the SAME 50 test scenes used for the Wilcoxon test (FR-006/SC-003), or a separate held-out set. If the same scenes, the Wilcoxon test (which tests for statistical difference) and the 1.18x threshold (which tests for practical equivalence) may conflict: the methods could be statistically different yet practically equivalent, or vice versa. Clarify the relationship between these two validation targets.

The Assumptions section states 'The feature graphs constructed from the DA3 dataset will fit within the ~7 GB RAM limit of the GitHub Actions free-tier runner when processed in batches.' This is a constraint on implementation, not a research assumption. A research assumption would be 'The feature graphs are sparse enough that k-NN construction scales linearly with scene count' or similar. Reframe this as an implementation constraint or move to a separate 'Implementation Constraints' section.

responses.response: Removed the circular validation by eliminating MSE as the fitting objective for FR-003. Instead, the filter is now optimized via a held-out validation set using Chamfer Distance (downstream metric), and US-1 Scenario 2 explicitly validates on held-out test scenes using Chamfer Distance against ground truth, breaking the circularity.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 now specifies optimization 'on held-out validation scenes using Chamfer Distance' instead of 'via Mean Squared Error on CPU'; US-1 Acceptance Scenario 2 now validates 'lower Chamfer Distance against ground truth on held-out test scenes' instead of MSE.

responses.response: Added Bonferroni multiple-comparison correction to US-2 Acceptance Scenario 2 and SC-005. The threshold is now p < 0.005 (corrected for ~10 tests), making the correlation analysis falsifiable. Null results (no eigenmode meeting the corrected threshold) are explicitly acceptable outcomes, addressing the near-unfalsifiability concern.
responses.what_changed: US-2 Acceptance Scenario 2 now specifies 'Bonferroni correction for ~10+ tests (threshold p < 0.005)'; SC-005 now states 'Bonferroni correction (threshold p < 0.005 for ~10 tests)' and clarifies that null results are acceptable outcomes.

responses.response: Corrected FR-007 and SC-004 to report variation in Chamfer Distance and MSE (actual outcome metrics) instead of false-positive/negative rates, which are undefined in a regression/denoising pipeline without classification labels.
responses.what_changed: FR-007 now specifies 'reporting the variation in Chamfer Distance and MSE across the sweep' instead of 'false-positive/negative rates'; SC-004 now states 'reporting the variation in Chamfer Distance and MSE across a sweep of cutoff parameters' instead of false-positive/negative rates.

responses.response: Replaced the paired t-test with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (non-parametric alternative suitable for non-normal, right-skewed distributions like Chamfer distances). The test is now two-tailed with α=0.05, and the hypothesis direction is explicitly stated: testing whether deterministic and diffusion methods produce statistically significantly different errors.
responses.what_changed: FR-006 now specifies 'Wilcoxon signed-rank test (non-parametric alternative to paired t-test, suitable for non-normal distributions)' with 'two-tailed test, α=0.05'; SC-003 now references the Wilcoxon test instead of t-test and clarifies the two-tailed hypothesis.

responses.response: Replaced the arbitrary 1.18x ratio with a principled interpolation definition: the deterministic method must achieve Chamfer Distance within the interval [noisy_baseline, diffusion_baseline], with performance ≥85% of the baseline's robustness gain defined as CD ≤ noisy_baseline + 0.15 × (diffusion_baseline - noisy_baseline). This grounds the '85% recovery' in the actual error landscape relative to both reference points.
responses.what_changed: SC-002 now defines '≥85% of the baseline's robustness' as 'CD ≤ noisy_baseline + 0.15 × (diffusion_baseline - noisy_baseline)' with explicit justification; US-3 Scenario 1 now uses this interpolation-based criterion instead of the 1.18x ratio.
